title: Architecture: Hosts, Clients, Transports
objective: After this lesson you will be able to map host/client/server roles, choose stdio vs Streamable HTTP transports, and trace the JSON-RPC discovery sequence (server/discover, _meta, capabilities) that opens every relationship.
why: MCP deployments fail at the seams teams skip: wrong transport for multi-client needs, missing discovery handling, confusion about who runs the model. The architecture is small (three roles, two transports, one discovery dance) — learn it exactly once from the spec (2026-07-28), and every later lesson's code has somewhere to live.

blocks.text: **Host**: the AI app (Claude Code, VS Code, your assistant) coordinating everything. **Client**: one per server connection, owned by the host — VS Code talking to filesystem + Sentry servers holds two clients. **Server**: exposes tools/resources/prompts over its connection. Models live in hosts; servers never see them directly (sampling, the old exception, is deprecated as of 2026-07-28 — servers needing completions call provider APIs).

blocks.caption: Host → N clients → N servers, one dedicated connection each

blocks.text: **stdio**: same-machine process I/O — one client, no network, minimal ops; stdout carries protocol (log to stderr!). **Streamable HTTP**: remote servers, many clients, standard HTTP auth (bearer/OAuth). Same JSON-RPC 2.0 messages either way — transport changes deployment and auth, never protocol semantics. Decide by locality + client count + auth needs.

rows: Streamable HTTP (remote, many clients, HTTP auth)
CI job calling one local tool

blocks.text: Every request carries `_meta` (protocolVersion 2026-07-28, clientCapabilities, clientInfo); every server must implement **`server/discover`** advertising versions + capabilities + identity. Clients *may* discover first or send directly and handle version errors. Stateless by design: servers infer nothing from history — each request self-describes. Version negotiation is explicit errors listing supported versions, not silent fallback.

blocks.caption: Stateless discovery: versions + capabilities negotiated per request metadata

blocks.title: Negotiate versions
blocks.note: Run it: agreed version, explicit version error listing server support, then highest-mutual selection. Negotiation is explicit errors, never silent fallback — the wire equivalent of fail-closed.

items: Host owns N clients (one per server); servers expose context; models live in hosts (sampling deprecated)
stdio: local single-client; Streamable HTTP: remote multi-client + HTTP auth; same JSON-RPC either way
server/discover + per-request _meta (version, capabilities, identity); stateless; explicit version errors

exercise.prompt: (a) Run the practice negotiator on all three cases and map outcomes. (b) Choose transports for: Claude Desktop + local catalog DB; backend serving 3 agent services with OAuth; CI lint job calling one local checker — with one-line reasons. (c) State what breaks if a stdio server logs to stdout.
hints: Outcomes: agreed 2026-07-28 / explicit UnsupportedProtocolVersion error / mutual fallback 2024-11-05.
Desktop+local → stdio (same machine, one client). Backend+OAuth → Streamable HTTP (remote, many, auth). CI → stdio (simplest).
stdout pollution corrupts JSON-RPC framing (parse failures on every message) — log to stderr/OpenTelemetry.
exercise.why: Transport choice (locality/clients/auth) plus wire hygiene (stdout discipline) plus version explicitness are the three deployment judgments — each practiced on concrete cases.
exercise.code: // Transport-decision pattern: locality + client count + auth → transport.

quiz.q: VS Code talks to filesystem + Sentry servers. Client count?
options: One per server (two clients) — dedicated connections per server
quiz.explain: Host owns N clients, one per server connection. Local stdio servers typically serve one client; remote HTTP serves many.

options: Streamable HTTP: remote multi-client with standard HTTP auth
quiz.explain: Remote + many clients + auth Sieg HTTP. Same-machine single-client would take stdio.

options: Explicit UnsupportedProtocolVersionError listing supported versions; client retries mutually supported
quiz.explain: Stateless explicitness extends to versions: errors name supported versions, clients negotiate openly. Never silent.

summary: Hosts own clients per server; transports by locality/clients/auth; discovery via server/discover with _meta everywhere; stdout is sacred. Spec 2026-07-28 throughout.
